[EFFECT] This is a binary step: 2012 (red, high value) receives a somewhat larger positive contribution than 2011 (blue, low value), and both sit on the positive side of the chart. The model has learned that demand grew from year one to year two, and it shifts the prediction upward accordingly for all 2012 hours.
[IMPORTANCE] Year is the second-ranked feature; its concentrated clusters show a consistent and sizeable positive shift, making it the strongest single-direction influence after hour.

---
[RECOMMENDATION] Staffing and bike-redistribution plans should be driven primarily by the **hour of the day** — which overwhelmingly determines whether a given hour will be busy or quiet — and secondarily by **temperature**, since warm spells can substantially lift demand even in off-peak hours. Scheduling more bikes and staff during warm, mid-to-late day hours will capture the greatest share of predicted demand variation.
